title.en: Running out of addresses, and choosing a route

description.en: Understand how NAT lets one public address serve a whole dorm, why IPv6 solves the shortage for good, what the three little helpers each do, and how routers use Dijkstra, distance vector and link state to work out which way to go.
description.zh: 懂得 NAT 怎样让一个公网地址养活整栋宿舍，IPv6 为什么能一劳永逸，三个小帮手各干什么，以及路由器怎样用 Dijkstra、距离向量和链路状态算出往哪走。

name.zh: 泛洪与广播路由 (flooding, broadcast routing, reverse path forwarding)

name.zh: 最短路径路由与 Dijkstra 算法 (shortest path routing)

name.zh: 距离向量与链路状态路由 (distance vector, link state)

description.en: Thinking a computer behind NAT can be connected to directly from outside. The translation table only has an entry once the internal host has sent a packet first.
description.zh: 以为 NAT 后面的电脑可以被外面的人直接连上。转换表只在内部主机先发包时才有条目。

description.en: Treating forwarding (looking up the table) and routing (building the table) as the same thing.
description.zh: 把转发（查表）和路由（建表）当成一回事。

description.en: Thinking shortest path routing is adaptive because it uses Dijkstra. What matters is whether the routes are recomputed as the network changes.
description.zh: 以为最短路径路由是自适应的，因为它用了 Dijkstra。看的是路由会不会随网络变化重新算。

description.en: When updating a distance vector, taking only the number the neighbour reports and forgetting to add the segment to that neighbour.
description.zh: 更新距离向量时只取邻居报告的数，忘了加上到这个邻居的那一段。

description.en: Thinking distance vector spreads good news and bad news equally fast. Bad news keeps counting upward (count to infinity).
description.zh: 以为距离向量对好消息和坏消息都传得一样快。坏消息会越数越大（无穷计数）。

description.en: Thinking reverse path forwarding needs to know the whole broadcast tree. It only looks at which line the packet came in on; it is a heuristic.
description.zh: 以为反向路径转发要知道整棵广播树。它只看包从哪条线来，是启发式。

description.en: Thinking hierarchical routing has only benefits. The tables get smaller, but the routes to some destinations get longer.
description.zh: 以为层次路由只有好处。表变小了，但有些目的地的路会变长。

chapter.en: What if there are not enough addresses?

title.en: One public address, a whole dorm
title.zh: 一个公网地址，一整栋宿舍

prompt.en: The dorm router has just one public IP address, 198.60.42.12, yet 4 devices in the dorm are online at the same time. The reply packet from a website carries only the destination address 198.60.42.12. When the router receives it, how does it know which device to hand it to?
prompt.zh: 宿舍路由器只有一个公网 IP 地址 198.60.42.12，可是宿舍里 4 台设备同时在上网。网站的回复包上只写着目的地址 198.60.42.12。路由器收到后，怎么知道该交给哪一台设备？

label.en: Copy the reply 4 times, send one to every device, and let each device pick
label.zh: 把回复包复制 4 份，每台设备都发一份，设备自己挑

feedback.en: A router does not broadcast like that. Every device would see everyone else's data, which is both wasteful and insecure.
feedback.zh: 路由器不会这样广播。那样每台设备都能看到别人的数据，既浪费又不安全。

label.en: Look at the port number in the reply: the router remembers “who started this port”
label.zh: 看回复包里的端口号：路由器记着「这个端口是谁发起的」

label.en: Each device actually has its own public IP, and the router sorts by IP
label.zh: 每台设备其实都有自己的公网 IP，路由器按 IP 分

feedback.en: The whole problem is that there are not enough public addresses to give one to every device.
feedback.zh: 问题恰恰是公网地址不够，每台设备一个根本给不起。

label.en: Hand it to one device at random, and let the wrong ones forward it on
label.zh: 随机交给其中一台，不对的设备再转发

feedback.en: Random delivery would scramble connections. Networks do not work this way.
feedback.zh: 随机会让连接乱掉，网络不会这样工作。

explain.en: An IP address can only identify “this dorm”, not the person inside. Telling people apart takes the transport-layer port number, and the router uses a table to remember which port belongs to whom. The next few pages are about that table.
explain.zh: IP 地址只能认出「这栋宿舍」，认不出里面的人。认人要靠传输层的端口号，路由器用一张表记住端口对应谁。下面几页就讲这张表。

title.en: Private addresses: house numbers every household can reuse
title.zh: 私有地址：各家各户可以重复用的门牌号

text.en: There are only $2^{32}$ IPv4 addresses, about 4.3 billion, which long ago stopped being enough (the address exhaustion in Lesson 9). The first remedy is to set aside three ranges of **private addresses**: they are never routed on the global Internet. Routers on the public Internet do not forward packets for these addresses and simply drop them, while the routers inside a home, a dorm or a campus forward them as usual. So every home, every dorm room and every university can reuse the same range, just as every neighbourhood can have its own “Building 3”.
text.zh: IPv4 地址只有 $2^{32}$，约 43 亿个，早就不够分了（第 9 课的地址耗尽）。第一个办法是留出三段**私有地址**（private IP addresses）：它们不会被路由到全球互联网。公网上的路由器不转发这些地址的包，收到就丢；家里、宿舍、学校内部的路由器却照常转发。所以每个家庭、每间宿舍、每所学校都可以重复使用同一段，就像每个小区都可以有「3 号楼」。

text.en: The numbers in the table count **addresses**, not hosts: in each block the first address (the network address) and the last (the broadcast address) cannot be given to hosts, so the usable hosts are 2 fewer.
text.zh: 表里的数字是**地址数**，不是主机数：每段里最前面的网络地址和最后面的广播地址不能分给主机，所以能用的主机要再减 2。

body.en: /12 fixes only the first 12 bits: the first byte is 172, and the first 4 bits of the second byte are 0001. The remaining 4 bits of the second byte can vary, from 16 to 31, which is 16 values, and each value has $2^{16}$ addresses under it, giving exactly $2^{20}$ in total. Written as /16, only 172.16.x.x would be left.
body.zh: /12 只固定前 12 位：第一个字节 172，第二个字节的前 4 位是 0001。第二个字节剩下 4 位可以变，从 16 到 31，一共 16 个值，每个值下面有 $2^{16}$ 个地址，合起来正好是 $2^{20}$。写成 /16 就只剩 172.16.x.x 了。

title.en: NAT: port numbers plus a translation table
title.zh: NAT：端口号加一张转换表

text.en: How does a host with a private address get onto the Internet? Through network address translation (NAT). The NAT box sits at the border between the inside network and the public Internet and maps many internal addresses onto **one** external address, telling connections apart by their TCP/UDP port numbers. Inside the box is a translation table that records “internal address plus port ↔ external port”.
text.zh: 私有地址的主机怎样上网？靠网络地址转换（NAT, network address translation）。NAT 盒子站在内网和公网的交界处，把许多内部地址映射到**一个**外部地址，用 TCP/UDP 端口号区分各条连接。盒子里有一张转换表，记着「内部地址加端口 ↔ 外部端口」。

alt.en: The NAT box translating in both directions: outbound, 10.0.0.1:5544 becomes 198.60.42.12:3344; on the way back, the table translates it back
alt.zh: NAT 盒子的双向翻译：出站时 10.0.0.1:5544 变成 198.60.42.12:3344，回程时按转换表翻回去

caption.en: Solid lines are outbound, dashed lines are the return path. A second device using the same local port 5544 is also given a different external port (for example 3345).
caption.zh: 实线是出站，虚线是回程。第二台设备用同样的本地端口 5544，也会被分到不同的外部端口（例如 3345）。

items.en: Outbound: a packet leaves 10.0.0.1 from port 5544. The NAT box rewrites the source address to 198.60.42.12, swaps the source port for an unused one, 3344, and records a row in the table.
items.zh: 出站：包从 10.0.0.1 端口 5544 发出，NAT 盒子把源地址改成 198.60.42.12，源端口换成一个没人用的 3344，并在表里记一行。

items.en: Return: the server's reply is sent to 198.60.42.12 port 3344. The box looks it up: 3344 corresponds to 10.0.0.1:5544, so it rewrites the address back and hands the packet to the inside network.
items.zh: 回程：服务器的回复发到 198.60.42.12 端口 3344。盒子查表，3344 对应 10.0.0.1:5544，改回去再交给内网。

items.en: It does not matter if two devices use the same local port: their external ports differ, so the table has two rows.
items.zh: 两台设备本地端口相同也没关系：外部端口不同，表里就是两行。

text.en: This approach has two costs. First, people outside cannot **initiate** a connection to the inside: table entries are created only when an inside host sends a packet first, so a packet coming in from outside finds no entry and the box does not know who to give it to. Second, it **breaks layering**: the IP layer is supposed to deal only with addresses, yet NAT has to change transport-layer ports; and some protocols write IP addresses into the data itself, which the box cannot fix when it only rewrites the header, so those protocols break.
text.zh: 这套办法有两个代价。第一，外面的人不能**主动**连里面：表里的条目是里面的主机先发包才建立的，外面主动发来的包找不到条目，盒子不知道交给谁。第二，它**违反分层原则**：IP 层本来只管地址，NAT 却要去改传输层的端口；还有些协议把 IP 地址写进了数据里，盒子改了包头却改不到数据，这些协议就会出问题。

title.en: Friends outside cannot connect
title.zh: 外面的朋友连不上

prompt.en: In your dorm you start a small game server on 10.0.0.1, listening on port 7000. The dorm has only one public address, 198.60.42.12. A friend off campus connects straight to 198.60.42.12:7000 and cannot get through. What is the most fundamental reason?
prompt.zh: 你在宿舍用 10.0.0.1 开了一个小游戏服务器，监听端口 7000。宿舍只有一个公网地址 198.60.42.12，朋友在校外直接连 198.60.42.12:7000，连不上。最根本的原因是什么？

label.en: The NAT box's translation table has no entry for this connection, so even when the packet reaches the box it does not know which inside host to give it to
label.zh: NAT 盒子的转换表里没有这条连接的条目，包到了盒子也不知道交给内网哪台主机

label.en: 10.0.0.1 is a private address, so your friend's packet cannot even reach your dorm router
label.zh: 10.0.0.1 是私有地址，朋友的包根本到不了你的宿舍路由器

feedback.en: Your friend's packet can reach the dorm router, because the public address 198.60.42.12 belongs to it. The problem arises after it gets into the box.
feedback.zh: 朋友的包能到宿舍路由器，因为公网地址 198.60.42.12 是它的。卡住的是进了盒子之后。

label.en: Port 7000 is higher than the largest port NAT can handle
label.zh: 端口 7000 超过了 NAT 能处理的最大端口

feedback.en: Ports range from 0 to 65535, so 7000 is fine.
feedback.zh: 端口范围是 0 到 65535，7000 没问题。

label.en: NAT only works for UDP, not for TCP
label.zh: NAT 只能用于 UDP，不能用于 TCP

feedback.en: NAT tells connections apart by port number for both TCP and UDP.
feedback.zh: NAT 对 TCP 和 UDP 都用端口号区分连接。

explain.en: Entries in the translation table are created when an inside host sends a packet first. A packet arriving unprompted from outside has no entry to look up, so the box has no way to translate it. To let people from outside connect in, you have to set a fixed mapping on the box by hand (port forwarding), or have the inside host connect out first.
explain.zh: 转换表的条目由内部主机先发包建立。外面主动来的包没有条目可查，盒子无从翻译。要让外面连进来，得手动在盒子上设一条固定的映射（端口转发），或者让内部主机先连出去。

hints.en: Where do the entries in the translation table come from?
hints.zh: 转换表里的条目是怎么来的？

chapter.en: IPv6 and the three little helpers

title.en: IPv6: just make the address longer
title.zh: IPv6：干脆把地址变长

text.en: Private addresses plus NAT only stretch what we have. The real cure is IPv6: addresses grow from 32 bits to 128 bits, giving $2^{128}\approx 3.4\times10^{38}$ addresses, so many that there is no need to economise. 128 bits = 16 bytes = 32 hexadecimal digits (one hex digit is 4 bits), written as 8 groups of 4 digits separated by colons.
text.zh: 私有地址加 NAT 只是省着用。治本的办法是 IPv6：地址从 32 位变成 128 位，地址数是 $2^{128}\approx 3.4\times10^{38}$，多到不必再省。128 位 = 16 字节 = 32 个十六进制数字（一个十六进制数字是 4 位），写成 8 组，每组 4 个数字，用冒号隔开。

text.en: That is long to write, so there are two abbreviation rules:
text.zh: 写起来太长，所以有两条缩写规则：

items.en: Leading 0s in each group can be dropped: 0074 becomes 74, and 0000 becomes 0.
items.zh: 每组前面的 0 可以省：0074 写成 74，0000 写成 0。

items.en: A run of all-zero groups can be replaced with `::`, which may be used **only once in the whole address**.
items.zh: 连续的全 0 组可以用 `::` 代替，**整个地址里只能用一次**。

text.en: The example above abbreviates to `FDEC:74::B0FF:0:FFFF`: the three consecutive 0000 groups in the middle become `::`, and the lone 0000 at the end becomes 0.
text.zh: 上面的例子缩写成 `FDEC:74::B0FF:0:FFFF`：中间连续三个 0000 变成 `::`，最后一个孤立的 0000 变成 0。

title.en: Why :: can be used only once
title.zh: 为什么 :: 只能用一次

body.en: An address has 8 groups in total. Given an abbreviated address, count how many groups are written, and the number missing is how many groups `::` stands for. With two of them, you could no longer tell how many groups each `::` stands for.
body.zh: 地址总共 8 组。看到缩写后的地址，数一数写了几组，缺的组数就是 `::` 代表的个数。用两次就算不出每个 `::` 各代表几组了。

title.en: The IPv6 header: simpler, so faster
title.zh: IPv6 头部：更简单，所以更快

alt.en: The IPv6 header: version, differentiated services, flow label; payload length, next header, hop limit; a 16-byte source address and a 16-byte destination address, 40 bytes in total
alt.zh: IPv6 头部：版本、区分服务、流标签，载荷长度、下一个头部、跳数限制，各 16 字节的源地址和目的地址，共 40 字节

caption.en: The header is a fixed 40 bytes.

items.en: **Flow label**: marks packets belonging to the same flow so routers treat the whole flow alike (for example a real-time audio or video stream).
items.zh: **流标签** Flow label：标记同一股数据流，让路由器对同一条流一视同仁（例如一路实时音视频）。

items.en: **Next header**: what follows, TCP, UDP, or an optional extension header. It corresponds to IPv4's Protocol.
items.zh: **下一个头部** Next header：后面跟的是什么，TCP、UDP，或者一个可选的扩展头部。对应 IPv4 的 Protocol。

items.en: **Hop limit**: decreased by 1 at every router and dropped when it reaches 0. It corresponds to IPv4's TTL.
items.zh: **跳数限制** Hop limit：每过一个路由器减 1，到 0 就丢。对应 IPv4 的 TTL。

items.en: **Payload length** and **Diff. services**: the length of the data part and the service class, respectively.
items.zh: **载荷长度** Payload length 和**区分服务** Diff. services：分别是数据部分的长度和服务等级。

text.en: Compared with the IPv4 header, IPv6 drops the header length (IHL), the header checksum and the fragmentation fields. The header is a fixed 40 bytes, routers do not need to compute a checksum, and they no longer fragment (fragmentation is left to the two ends, see path MTU discovery in Lesson 8), so processing is faster. When extra features are needed, extension headers are chained on behind.
text.zh: 和 IPv4 头部比，IPv6 去掉了头部长度（IHL）、头部校验和和分片字段。头部固定 40 字节，路由器不用算校验和，也不用再分片（分片留给两端，第 8 课的路径 MTU 发现），处理起来更快。需要额外功能时，用扩展头部挂在后面。

text.en: The world cannot switch to IPv6 overnight, so there are three transition methods: **dual stack** means a device runs IPv4 and IPv6 at the same time; **tunneling** wraps an IPv6 packet inside an IPv4 packet to cross a network that only understands IPv4 (tunnels came up in Lesson 8); **header translation** rewrites one kind of header into the other at the boundary. IPv6 was also designed to support encryption and authentication (IPsec, covered in Lesson 19) directly.
text.zh: 世界不可能一夜之间全换成 IPv6，所以有三种过渡办法：**双栈**（dual stack）是一台设备同时跑 IPv4 和 IPv6；**隧道**（tunneling）是把 IPv6 包装进 IPv4 包，穿过只懂 IPv4 的网络（第 8 课讲过隧道）；**头部翻译**（header translation）是在边界上把一种头部改写成另一种。IPv6 在设计时也把加密和认证（IPsec，第 19 课展开）当成可以直接支持的功能。

title.en: Abbreviate an address
title.zh: 缩写一个地址

prompt.en: Abbreviate 2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0001 by the rules. Which of these is correct?

feedback.en: `::` is there to replace a run of all-zero groups. The zeros are already written out, and adding `::` at the end makes the group count come out wrong.
feedback.zh: `::` 的作用是替代连续的全 0 组。已经把 0 写出来了，又在末尾加 `::`，算出来组数就对不上了。

feedback.en: `::` may be used only once in the whole address, otherwise you cannot tell how many groups each `::` stands for.
feedback.zh: `::` 整个地址里只能用一次，否则无法确定每个 `::` 代表几组。

feedback.en: Only leading 0s may be dropped. 0db8 becomes db8; you cannot also drop the d in the middle.
feedback.zh: 只能省前导 0。0db8 省成 db8，不能把中间的 d 也省掉。

explain.en: Removing the leading 0 from 0db8 gives db8; the five consecutive all-zero groups after it become a single `::`; and the last group 0001 loses its leading zeros to give 1.
explain.zh: 0db8 去掉前导 0 得 db8；后面连续五个全 0 组换成一个 `::`；最后一组 0001 去前导 0 得 1。

hints.en: Leading 0s can only be dropped from the start of a group, not digits from the middle.
hints.zh: 前导 0 只能省组的开头，不能省中间的数字。

title.en: What the IPv6 header looks like
title.zh: IPv6 头部长什么样

prompt.en: Which of these statements about the IPv6 header is correct?
prompt.zh: 下面哪一句对 IPv6 头部的描述是对的？

label.en: The header is a fixed 40 bytes, with no IHL and no header checksum
label.zh: 头部固定 40 字节，没有 IHL，也没有头部校验和

label.en: There is no field like TTL; loops are prevented with the header checksum instead
label.zh: 没有 TTL 这样的字段，防环路改用头部校验和

feedback.en: TTL has not disappeared. It was renamed Hop limit, still decreased by 1 at every router and dropped at 0. The checksum has nothing to do with preventing loops.
feedback.zh: TTL 没有消失，改名叫跳数限制 (Hop limit)，每过一个路由器照样减 1，到 0 就丢。校验和和防环路没有关系。

label.en: The header length can still vary, so IHL was kept
label.zh: 头部长度仍然可变，所以保留了 IHL

feedback.en: The IPv6 header is a fixed 40 bytes, so IHL is not needed. When extra features are needed, extension headers are chained on behind.
feedback.zh: IPv6 头部固定 40 字节，所以不需要 IHL。需要额外功能时，用扩展头部挂在后面。

label.en: There is no protocol field; routers recognise TCP and UDP from the port number
label.zh: 没有协议字段，路由器靠端口号认出 TCP 和 UDP

feedback.en: Protocol has not disappeared. It was renamed Next header, and says whether TCP, UDP or an extension header follows. Port numbers live at the transport layer, which the IP layer cannot see.
feedback.zh: Protocol 没有消失，改名叫下一个头部 (Next header)，说明后面是 TCP、UDP 还是扩展头部。端口号在传输层，IP 层看不到。

explain.en: IPv6 drops the header length IHL, the header checksum and the fragmentation fields, and the header is a fixed 40 bytes: the link-layer CRC and the transport-layer checksum already guard the data, so routers need not recompute one at every hop, which makes processing faster. TTL and Protocol were simply renamed, to Hop limit and Next header.
explain.zh: IPv6 去掉了头部长度 IHL、头部校验和和分片字段，头部固定 40 字节：链路层的 CRC 和传输层的校验和已经把关，路由器不必每一跳再算一遍，处理更快。TTL 和 Protocol 只是改了名，分别叫跳数限制和下一个头部。

title.en: ICMP: the messenger for IP
title.zh: ICMP：IP 的报信员

text.en: IP only does its best to deliver and does not tell you when something goes wrong. IP's partner ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol) is there to bring the news: its messages **travel inside IP packets** and tell the source host what happened along the way.
text.zh: IP 只管尽力送，出了岔子不会告诉你。IP 的伙伴 ICMP（Internet Control Message Protocol）专门负责报信：它的消息**装在 IP 包里**传，告诉源主机路上出了什么事。

rows.en: Tells a router there is a closer route
rows.zh: 告诉路由器有更近的路

rows.en: A timestamped echo, finding nearby routers
rows.zh: 带时间戳的回显、找附近的路由器

rows.en: Asks the sender to slow down (deprecated)
rows.zh: 要求发送方慢点（已被弃用）

text.en: **ping**: send an Echo, the other side replies with an Echo reply, and the round-trip time is the round-trip delay.
text.zh: **ping**：发一个 Echo，对方回 Echo reply，来回时间就是往返延迟。

text.en: **traceroute** uses TTL cleverly: first send a packet with TTL=1, and the first router decrements the TTL to 0, drops the packet and sends back a Time exceeded, so the first router gives itself away; then send TTL=2, and the second router gives itself away; and so on, until the packet reaches the destination host. The probe is deliberately sent to a port nobody is listening on, so the destination host replies not with Time exceeded but with Destination unreachable (specifically “port unreachable”): seeing that tells you you have arrived. Strung together, these replies are the path your packet took.
text.zh: **traceroute** 利用 TTL 的巧妙办法：先发 TTL=1 的包，第一个路由器把 TTL 减成 0，丢掉它并回一个 Time exceeded，于是第一个路由器暴露了自己；再发 TTL=2，第二个路由器暴露；依此类推，直到包到达目的主机。探测包故意发给一个没人监听的端口，所以目的主机回的不是 Time exceeded，而是 Destination unreachable（具体是「端口不可达」）：看到它，就知道到终点了。把这些回信连起来，就是你的包走过的路。

body.en: A ping-based traceroute instead probes with Echo, and the end is marked by an Echo reply. Source quench was an early message for asking the sender to slow down and is no longer used; slowing down is now left to TCP's congestion control (Lesson 13). Destination unreachable is also used to signal “packet too big and not allowed to be fragmented”, which is what path MTU discovery in Lesson 8 relies on.
body.zh: 基于 ping 的 traceroute 则用 Echo 做探测，终点以 Echo reply 收尾。Source quench 是早期让发送方降速的消息，现在已不再使用，降速交给 TCP 的拥塞控制（第 13 课）。Destination unreachable 还会用来通知「包太大且不许分片」，这就是第 8 课路径 MTU 发现的依据。

title.en: ARP and DHCP: finding the MAC, getting an address
title.zh: ARP 和 DHCP：找 MAC，要地址

text.en: Your laptop has just joined the dorm Wi-Fi: it has no IP address yet and does not know where the gateway is. Two helpers pass the baton.
text.zh: 你的笔记本刚连上宿舍 Wi-Fi：它还没有 IP 地址，也不知道网关在哪。有两个帮手接力。

text.en: DHCP: get an IP automatically
text.zh: DHCP：自动领一个 IP

text.en: DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol; the slides write Control, but it should be Configuration) lets a host configure its network settings automatically. It is a four-step conversation:
text.zh: DHCP（Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol；课件写成 Control，应是 Configuration）让主机自动配好网络设置。它是一段四步对话：

items.en: **Discover**: the laptop broadcasts to the whole network, “Is there a DHCP server?”
items.zh: **发现** Discover：笔记本向全网广播「有 DHCP 服务器吗？」。

items.en: **Offer**: a server replies, “Here is an address for you.”
items.zh: **提供** Offer：服务器回「给你这个地址」。

items.en: **Request**: the laptop answers, “Good, I will take that one.”
items.zh: **请求** Request：笔记本回「好，我就要这个」。

items.en: **Acknowledge**: the server confirms.
items.zh: **确认** Acknowledge：服务器确认。

text.en: What it hands out is not a permanent address but a **lease** with a time limit, which must be renewed before it expires. Besides the IP address, DHCP also supplies the subnet mask, the default gateway and the DNS server address (you will use that last one in Lesson 14).
text.zh: 给出的不是永久地址，而是有期限的**租约**（lease），到期前要续约。除了 IP 地址，DHCP 还会给子网掩码、默认网关和 DNS 服务器地址（第 14 课你会用到这最后一个）。

text.en: ARP: know the IP, find the MAC
text.zh: ARP：已知 IP，求 MAC

text.en: The link layer delivers by MAC address (Lesson 7), while IP only knows IP addresses. To hand a packet to the gateway, the laptop first has to know the gateway's MAC. So ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) broadcasts on the local network, “Who is 192.168.1.1?”, and the owner of that address answers with its MAC address. The answer is cached for a while, so next time there is no need to ask.
text.zh: 链路层按 MAC 地址投递（第 7 课），IP 只知道 IP 地址。笔记本要把包交给网关，得先知道网关的 MAC。于是 ARP（Address Resolution Protocol）在局域网里广播一句「谁是 192.168.1.1？」，地址的主人回答自己的 MAC 地址。答案会缓存一阵，下次不用再问。

title.en: The first moment after joining Wi-Fi
title.zh: 刚连上 Wi-Fi 的第一刻

prompt.en: Your laptop has just joined the dorm Wi-Fi, has no IP, and does not know the gateway's MAC. To send the first packet to www.unimelb.edu.au, in what order are the protocols used?
prompt.zh: 你的笔记本刚连上宿舍 Wi-Fi，还没有 IP，也不知道网关的 MAC。要发出访问 www.unimelb.edu.au 的第一个包，几个协议用到的先后顺序是？

label.en: First DHCP to get an IP, gateway address and DNS, then ARP to ask for the gateway's MAC, and only then can the packet be sent
label.zh: 先 DHCP 领到 IP、网关地址和 DNS，再 ARP 问网关的 MAC，然后才能发包

label.en: First ARP to ask for the gateway's MAC, then DHCP to get an IP
label.zh: 先 ARP 问网关的 MAC，再 DHCP 领 IP

feedback.en: An ARP request must include your own IP address, so you cannot ask without one. And without the gateway's IP you would not know whom to ask.
feedback.zh: ARP 请求里要写上自己的 IP 地址，没有 IP 就问不了。而且不知道网关的 IP，也不知道该问谁。

label.en: First ping the gateway (ICMP) to check that it is online, then do everything else
label.zh: 先 ping 一下网关（ICMP）确认它在线，再做别的

feedback.en: A ping is itself carried in an IP packet. Without an IP and the gateway's MAC, you cannot even send a ping.
feedback.zh: ping 本身也是装在 IP 包里的，没有 IP 和网关的 MAC，连 ping 都发不出去。

label.en: Only DHCP is needed; the gateway discovers the MAC address by itself
label.zh: 只需要 DHCP，MAC 地址由网关自己发现

feedback.en: The link layer delivers by MAC, so the sender must first know the gateway's MAC, and that is exactly what ARP is for.
feedback.zh: 链路层必须靠 MAC 投递，发送方得先知道网关的 MAC，ARP 就是干这个的。

explain.en: DHCP answers “who am I, and who is the gateway”; ARP answers “what is the gateway's physical address”. With those two, the packet can leave your network card.
explain.zh: DHCP 解决「我是谁、网关是谁」，ARP 解决「网关的物理地址是什么」。有了这两样，包才能从你的网卡发出去。

chapter.en: Routing: how do we know which way to go?

title.en: Forwarding is looking up a table; routing is building it
title.zh: 转发是查表，路由是建表

text.en: When a router receives a packet, it does two different jobs, which the slides often blur together:
text.zh: 路由器收到一个包，要做两件不同的事，课件常把它们混在一起：

items.en: **Forwarding**: look at the destination address in the packet header, look it up in the router's own routing table, and decide which line to send it out on. One table lookup, very fast.
items.zh: **转发**（forwarding）：看包头的目的地址，查自己的路由表，决定从哪条线发出去。一次查表，很快。

items.en: **Routing**: how that table gets **built** and updated as the network changes. The algorithms in the second half of this lesson are all doing this.
items.zh: **路由**（routing）：怎样把这张表**建出来**、并在网络变化时更新。这一课后半讲的算法都在干这件事。

text.en: The approach is to view the network as a graph: routers are nodes, links are edges, and each edge has a cost, which can be hops, delay and so on. A routing algorithm finds, for every destination, the best next hop on the graph (the “line” column in the table).
text.zh: 做法是把网络看成一张图：路由器是结点，链路是边，每条边有代价，可以是跳数、延迟等。路由算法就是在图上为每个目的地找出最好的下一跳（表里的「线路」一列）。

text.en: Algorithms fall into two broad classes. **Non-adaptive** (static routing): routes are computed in advance and not recomputed as the network changes. **Adaptive** (dynamic): routes are recomputed as topology and traffic change. The difference is not which algorithm is used, but whether the routes **get updated as the network changes**.
text.zh: 算法分两大类。**非自适应**（non-adaptive，静态路由）：路由事先算好，不随网络变化重新算。**自适应**（adaptive，动态）：会随拓扑、流量的变化重新计算。区别不在于用了什么算法，而在于路由**会不会随网络变化而更新**。

rows.en: Hierarchical routing (growing scale), broadcast routing (one to many)
rows.zh: 层次路由（规模变大）、广播路由（一对多）

title.en: Why is shortest path non-adaptive?
title.zh: 最短路径为什么是非自适应的？

body.en: Link state routing, coming later, also uses Dijkstra, yet it is adaptive. The difference: link state keeps collecting link information and recomputing, while plain shortest path routing computes once and afterwards does not care whether the network changes.
body.zh: 后面的链路状态路由也用 Dijkstra，却是自适应的。差别在于：链路状态会不断重新收集链路信息、重新算；纯粹的最短路径路由只算一次，之后不管网络变不变。

title.en: Two routers: which one is adaptive?
title.zh: 两台路由器，哪一台是自适应

prompt.en: Both routers use Dijkstra to compute their routing tables. Router A computes only once, at power-on, and its table never changes afterwards; Router B recomputes every time it receives new link state information. After a link goes down, which one is using an adaptive algorithm?
prompt.zh: 两台路由器都用 Dijkstra 算出路由表。甲只在开机时算一次，之后表一直不变；乙每次收到新的链路状态信息，就重新算一遍。一条链路断了之后，哪一台属于自适应算法？

label.en: B: its routes are recomputed as the network changes
label.zh: 乙：它的路由会随网络变化重新计算

label.en: A: Dijkstra is a shortest path algorithm, and shortest path means adaptive
label.zh: 甲：Dijkstra 是最短路径算法，最短路径就是自适应的

feedback.en: The name of the algorithm does not decide the class. Once A has computed, it never updates, so it would not know the network had changed: it is non-adaptive.
feedback.zh: 算法的名字不决定类别。甲算完就不再更新，网络变了它也不知道，是非自适应的。

label.en: Both, because both use Dijkstra
label.zh: 两台都是，因为都用了 Dijkstra

feedback.en: What counts is not which algorithm is used but whether the routes are updated as the network changes.
feedback.zh: 看的不是用了什么算法，而是路由会不会随网络变化而更新。

label.en: Neither, because Dijkstra is always static
label.zh: 两台都不是，因为 Dijkstra 总是静态的

feedback.en: Dijkstra is just one step for computing shortest paths. Link state routing reruns it every time new information arrives, and is adaptive.
feedback.zh: Dijkstra 只是一个算最短路径的步骤。链路状态路由每次收到新信息就重跑它，是自适应的。

explain.en: Whether something is adaptive depends on “whether the routes are updated as topology and traffic change”. A computes once and then ignores the network, so it is non-adaptive; B recomputes as soon as it notices a change, so it is adaptive. The same Dijkstra can appear in non-adaptive shortest path routing and also in adaptive link state routing.
explain.zh: 自适应与否，看的是「路由会不会随拓扑、流量的变化而更新」。甲算一次就不管了，是非自适应；乙一发现变化就重算，是自适应。同样的 Dijkstra，既可以出现在非自适应的最短路径路由里，也可以出现在自适应的链路状态路由里。

title.en: The optimality principle and the sink tree
title.zh: 最优性原理与汇集树

text.en: If router B is on the optimal path from A to C, then the optimal path from B to C must be exactly the rest of that path.
text.zh: 如果路由器 B 在 A 到 C 的最优路径上，那么 B 到 C 的最优路径一定就是这条路径剩下的那一段。

text.en: By contradiction: let the route from A to B be $r_1$, and the second half of the optimal path from A to C through B be $r_2$. If B actually has a better route $r_3$ to C, then going from A through B along $r_1+r_3$ would be better than $r_1+r_2$, contradicting the claim that $r_1+r_2$ is optimal. So there is no better $r_3$.
text.zh: 用反证法：设 A 到 B 的路是 $r_1$，A 经 B 到 C 的最优路径后半段是 $r_2$。如果 B 到 C 其实有更好的 $r_3$，那么 A 经 B 走 $r_1+r_3$ 就比 $r_1+r_2$ 更好，和「$r_1+r_2$ 最优」矛盾。所以不存在更好的 $r_3$。

text.en: Let us plug in numbers: $r_1$ costs 2 and $r_2$ costs 3, so the whole trip costs 2+3 = 5, the optimum from A to C. Suppose B also had an $r_3$ to C costing only 1. Then A going through B along $r_1+r_3$ would cost only 2+1 = 3, less than 5, so 5 would not be optimal after all, a contradiction. So such an $r_3$ cannot exist.
text.zh: 代入数字看看：$r_1$ 花 2，$r_2$ 花 3，全程 2+3 = 5，是 A 到 C 的最优。假如 B 到 C 还有一条 $r_3$ 只花 1，A 经 B 走 $r_1+r_3$ 全程只要 2+1 = 3，比 5 小，5 就不是最优了，矛盾。所以这样的 $r_3$ 不存在。

text.en: The corollary is very useful: put together the optimal paths from **all** sources to one destination and they form a tree rooted at that destination, called the **sink tree**. Every router following the tree toward the root is on its optimal path. The goal of a routing algorithm is to discover and use this tree for every destination. Below is a small network of five routers, rooted at D.
text.zh: 推论很有用：把**所有**源到某个目的地的最优路径合起来，会形成一棵以目的地为根的树，叫**汇集树**（sink tree）。每个路由器沿着树往根走就是最优路径。路由算法的目标，就是为每个目的地发现并用上这棵树。下面是一个五个路由器的小网络，以 D 为根。

alt.zh: 五个路由器 A、B、C、D、E 的网络，权重 A-B 2、B-D 1、C-D 1、E-C 2、A-C 4、E-B 3；以 D 为根的汇集树用粗线画出：A-B-D 和 E-C-D，A 的距离 3，E 的距离 3

caption.en: A's optimal path is A-B-D and E's is E-C-D; the two lines A-C and E-B are not in the tree.
caption.zh: A 的最优路径是 A-B-D，E 的是 E-C-D；A-C 和 E-B 两条线不在树里。

items.en: It is a tree, so it has **no loops**: each router has exactly one next hop toward the root, and every step along the tree reduces the distance to the root by a positive weight, so you can never wind up back where you started.
items.zh: 它是树，所以**没有环**：每个路由器只有一个去根的下一跳，每沿树走一步，到根的距离就少一段正的权重，不可能绕回原地。

items.en: It is **not necessarily unique**: if two routes have equal weight, there is more than one tree. We will meet this in the Dijkstra example below.
items.zh: 它**不一定唯一**：如果两条路权重相等，就有不止一棵。下面 Dijkstra 的例子里就会遇到。

title.en: Change a weight and the tree follows
title.zh: 权重一变，树跟着变

prompt.en: Using the network in the figure above: A–B 2, B–D 1, C–D 1, A–C 4, E–C 2, E–B 3. Now change only the weight of B–D from 1 to 6 and recompute the sink tree rooted at D. For packets from A to D, what does the next hop become?
prompt.zh: 沿用上图的网络：A–B 2、B–D 1、C–D 1、A–C 4、E–C 2、E–B 3。现在只把 B–D 的权重从 1 改成 6，重新算以 D 为根的汇集树。A 发往 D 的包，下一跳变成谁？

label.en: Still B; the sink tree does not change just because one link's weight changes
label.zh: 还是 B，汇集树不会因为一条链路的权重改变而变

feedback.en: The sink tree is computed from the weights. Once B–D becomes expensive, the total distance to D via B becomes 2+6 = 8, which is more than the alternative, so the tree has to be recomputed.
feedback.zh: 汇集树是由权重算出来的。B–D 变贵之后，经 B 到 D 的总距离变成 2+6 = 8，比别的路贵，树要重算。

label.en: Still B, because A–B is only 2, smaller than A–C's 4
label.zh: 还是 B，因为 A–B 只有 2，比 A–C 的 4 小

feedback.en: You cannot choose the next hop by looking only at the first segment; you have to look at the total distance to the root: via B it is 2+6 = 8, via C it is 4+1 = 5.
feedback.zh: 选下一跳不能只看第一段，要看到根的总距离：经 B 是 2+6 = 8，经 C 是 4+1 = 5。

feedback.en: There is no link between A and E, so the next hop must be one of A's neighbours (B or C).
feedback.zh: A 和 E 之间没有链路，下一跳必须是 A 的邻居 (B 或 C)。

explain.en: Recompute the distances with D as the root: C is 1, E via C is 1+2 = 3, A via C is 4+1 = 5, via B it is 2+6 = 8, so take 5. A's parent in the tree becomes C, and the next hop is C.
explain.zh: 重新算以 D 为根的距离：C 是 1，E 经 C 是 1+2 = 3，A 经 C 是 4+1 = 5，经 B 是 2+6 = 8，取 5。所以 A 在树里的父结点变成 C，下一跳是 C。

hints.en: First work out each node's distance to D. A has two neighbours to choose from; compute the total distance through each.
hints.zh: 先算每个结点到 D 的距离。A 有两个邻居可选，各算一次总距离。

title.en: Dijkstra: growing the tree outward from the destination, ring by ring
title.zh: Dijkstra：从终点向外一圈圈长出这棵树

text.en: How do we actually compute this tree? Give each link a **non-negative** weight; the shortest path is the path with the smallest total weight. Make every weight 1 and it is the fewest hops. Why are “the shortest paths from A to everyone” and “the sink tree of everyone to A” the same thing? Because links are symmetric in both directions, computing outward from A is equivalent to computing the tree of everyone to A.
text.zh: 怎样真的算出这棵树？给每条链路一个**非负**权重，最短路径就是总权重最小的路径。全取 1，就是跳数最少。为什么「A 到别人的最短路径」和「别人到 A 的汇集树」是一回事？因为链路是双向对称的，从 A 往外算，等价于算所有人到 A 的树。

text.en: Dijkstra's idea: first fix the node closest to the destination, then use it to update the others, expanding outward ring by ring. Two things need to be tracked: the set P (nodes already settled and added to the tree) and each node's $d$ (the shortest distance to the destination known so far).
text.zh: Dijkstra 的想法是：先确定离终点最近的结点，再用它去更新别人，一圈圈往外扩。要记两样东西：集合 P（已经定下来、加入树的结点）和每个结点的 $d$（目前已知到终点的最短距离）。

items.en: P starts empty; every node other than the destination has $d=\infty$, and the destination has $d=0$.
items.zh: P 开始为空，除终点外每个结点的 $d=\infty$，终点的 $d=0$。

items.en: As long as P does not contain every node: among the nodes not in P, pick the node $v$ with the smallest $d$ and add it to P.
items.zh: 只要 P 没包含所有结点：在不在 P 里的结点中，选 $d$ 最小的结点 $v$ 加入 P。

items.en: Update each neighbour $u$ of $v$: if $d(v)+w(v,u)<d(u)$, set $d(u)$ to this smaller value and record that $u$'s previous node is $v$. Update only when strictly smaller; on a tie, leave it.
items.zh: 更新 $v$ 的每个邻居 $u$：如果 $d(v)+w(v,u)<d(u)$，就把 $d(u)$ 改成这个更小的值，并记下 $u$ 的上一个结点是 $v$。更小才更新，相等不改。

title.en: Why weights must be non-negative
title.zh: 为什么权重必须非负

body.en: When we pick the node with the smallest $d$, we declare it already optimal, because a detour later can only make the distance larger or equal. With a negative weight, going around could actually be shorter, and that declaration no longer holds.
body.zh: 选出 $d$ 最小的结点时，我们认定它已经最优，因为以后绕路只会让距离更大或相等。如果有负权重，绕一圈反而可能更短，这个认定就不成立了。

title.en: A step-by-step walk-through: with A as the destination
title.zh: 逐步走一遍：以 A 为终点

text.en: The graph has 8 nodes, with weights: AB 2, AG 6, BC 7, BE 2, EG 1, EF 2, CF 3, CD 3, FH 2, DH 2, GH 4. A is the destination. On each row: first pick the node with the smallest $d$, then update its neighbours.
text.zh: 图有 8 个结点，权重：AB 2、AG 6、BC 7、BE 2、EG 1、EF 2、CF 3、CD 3、FH 2、DH 2、GH 4。以 A 为终点。每一行：先选 $d$ 最小的结点，再更新它的邻居。

H=6+2=8, smaller than 9, so change it; C=6+3=9, equal to the existing 9, so leave it
rows.zh: H=6+2=8，比 9 小，改；C=6+3=9，和现有的 9 相等，不改

rows.en: D=9+3=12, not smaller than 10, so leave it

text.en: How do we get the routing table? Look at each node's “previous node”, which is its parent in the tree, and that is its **first hop** toward A. D's path is D→H→F→E→B→A, so in D's table the “line” entry for A is H. The (2, A) in the slides' figure means “distance 2, previous node A”.
text.zh: 怎么得到路由表？看每个结点「上一个结点」，也就是树上它的父亲，那就是它走向 A 的**第一跳**。D 的路径是 D→H→F→E→B→A，所以 D 的表里去 A 的「线路」一列写 H。课件图里的 (2, A) 就是「距离 2，上一个结点 A」。

title.en: The sink tree is not unique
title.zh: 汇集树不唯一

body.en: C via B is 2+7=9, and via F is 6+3=9, a tie. Either choice is correct, and this is why the sink tree is not unique.
body.zh: C 经 B 是 2+7=9，经 F 是 6+3=9，打平了。选哪条都对，这就是汇集树不唯一的原因。

title.en: Work it out by hand
title.zh: 手算一遍

prompt.en: Four routers A, B, C, D with link weights: A–B 3, A–C 1, C–B 1, B–D 2, C–D 5. Run Dijkstra with A as the destination. What is the shortest distance from D to A?
prompt.zh: 四个路由器 A、B、C、D，链路权重：A–B 3，A–C 1，C–B 1，B–D 2，C–D 5。以 A 为终点用 Dijkstra 算，D 到 A 的最短距离是多少？

explain.en: Steps: pick A (0) and update B=3, C=1. Pick C (1) and update B=1+1=2 (smaller than 3, so change it), D=1+5=6. Pick B (2) and update D=2+2=4 (smaller than 6, so change it). Pick D (4). The path is D→B→C→A, total weight 2+1+1=4. Looking only at A–B's 3 would miss the 2 you get by going around through C.
explain.zh: 步骤：选 A（0），更新 B=3，C=1。选 C（1），更新 B=1+1=2（比 3 小，改），D=1+5=6。选 B（2），更新 D=2+2=4（比 6 小，改）。选 D（4）。路径是 D→B→C→A，总权重 2+1+1=4。直接看 A–B 的 3 会错过经 C 绕过去的 2。

hints.en: Always pick the node with the smallest d, and after each pick check whether any neighbour can be lowered.
hints.zh: 先选 d 最小的结点，每次选完都检查邻居能不能被改小。

title.en: Flooding: the dumbest and also the most robust way
title.zh: 泛洪：最笨也最稳的办法

text.en: Flooding needs no routing table at all: every incoming packet is sent out on **every outgoing line except the one it came in on**. As long as there is any path between two points, the packet is sure to arrive, so it is very robust.
text.zh: 泛洪（flooding）不需要任何路由表：每个进来的包，从**除了来路之外的每条出线**都发出去。只要两点之间有一条通路，包就一定能到，所以它很健壮。

text.en: The cost is far too many duplicate packets. Imagine 4 routers all connected to each other: source A sends out 3 copies; B, C and D each forward the packet to their other two neighbours (not back where it came from), giving 6 more copies, then 12 in the next round, and so on. Without limits, packets circle in loops forever. There are two remedies:
text.zh: 代价是重复的包太多。设想 4 个路由器两两相连，源 A 发出 3 份；B、C、D 各把包转给另外两个邻居（不转回来路），又是 6 份，下一轮 12 份……不加限制，包永远在环里打转。办法有两个：

items.en: **A hop counter**: decreased by 1 at every router and dropped at 0.
items.zh: **跳数计数器**：每过一个路由器减 1，到 0 就丢。

items.en: **Sequence numbers**: each source numbers its packets, and routers remember what they have seen, forwarding a duplicate from the same source only once.
items.zh: **序号**：每个源给包编序号，路由器记住见过的，同一个源的重复包只转发一次。

text.en: Selective flooding goes a step further: send only on lines that point roughly in the right direction. Flooding is not suited to everyday forwarding, but it suits two situations: when a message absolutely must get through (such as the link state packets in link state routing below), and broadcast.
text.zh: 选择性泛洪（selective flooding）更进一步：只往大致方向正确的线路发。泛洪不适合日常转发，但适合两种场合：要保证消息一定送到（比如下面链路状态里的链路状态包），以及广播。

title.en: Distance vector: just ask your neighbours
title.zh: 距离向量：只问邻居

text.en: Each router knows only its own neighbours, yet wants to know how far away every place in the network is. The method is plain: ask a neighbour, “How far are you from there?”, then add the segment from yourself to that neighbour. Nobody needs to know the whole graph.
text.zh: 每个路由器只认识自己的邻居，却想知道到全网每个地方最短有多远。办法很朴素：问邻居「你到那儿多远？」，再加上自己走到这个邻居的一段。谁都不用知道整张图。

text.en: Each router keeps a table recording the lowest known distance to every destination and which line to use. The algorithm has four steps:
text.zh: 每个路由器维护一张表，记着到每个目的地的已知最低距离，和用哪条线去。算法有四步：

items.en: Know the distance to each neighbour.
items.zh: 知道到每个邻居的距离。

items.en: Advertise your own **distance vector** (the lowest distances to all destinations) to all neighbours.
items.zh: 把自己的**距离向量**（到各个目的地的最低距离）通告给所有邻居。

items.en: Update your own vector from the vectors you receive.
items.zh: 根据收到的向量，更新自己的向量。

items.en: Repeat periodically, to keep up with changes in the network.
items.zh: 周期性地重复，跟上网络的变化。

text.en: Global information is shared only between neighbours, layer by layer. The update formula for step 3 is:
text.zh: 全局的信息，只在邻居之间一层层共享。第 3 步的更新公式是：

text.en: How to read it: the new distance to X is computed as a candidate for each neighbour N, equal to “the segment to N, $c(N)$” plus “the distance N reports to X, $D_N(X)$”; take the smallest of them. Whichever neighbour gives the minimum is the one written as the line toward X.
text.zh: 读法：到 X 的新距离，对每个邻居 N 算一个候选值，是「走到 N 的这一段 $c(N)$」加上「N 报告的它到 X 的距离 $D_N(X)$」；取其中最小的。最小值来自哪个邻居，去 X 的线路就写哪个邻居。

title.en: Work it out: router J's new vector
title.zh: 算一遍：路由器 J 的新向量

intro.en: Router J has four neighbours A, I, H, K, and the delays (in milliseconds) to them are 8, 10, 12, 6. The distances to G advertised by the neighbours are 18, 31, 6, 31 respectively. Let us see how J computes its new distance to G.
intro.zh: 路由器 J 有四个邻居 A、I、H、K，到它们的延迟（毫秒）是 8、10、12、6。邻居通告的到 G 的距离分别是 18、31、6、31。看 J 怎样算到 G 的新距离。

why.en: For each neighbour N, the distance to G is “J to N” plus “N to G”; take the smallest.
why.zh: 对每个邻居 N，到 G 的距离是「J 到 N」加「N 到 G」，取最小。

why.en: The four neighbours A, I, H, K each give one candidate.
why.zh: A、I、H、K 四个邻居各给出一个候选值。

why.en: Going through H is smallest, so J's table writes distance 18 to G, with line H.
why.zh: 经 H 最小，所以 J 的表里去 G 写距离 18，线路 H。

outro.en: Working out J's whole new vector the same way gives (distance, line; the numbers are delays in milliseconds): A 8 A, B 20 A, C 28 I, D 20 H, E 17 I, F 30 I, G 18 H, H 12 H, I 10 I, K 6 K, L 15 K. For example, to D: via A is 8+40=48, via I is 10+27=37, via H is 12+8=20, via K is 6+24=30, so take 20.
outro.zh: 同样算出 J 的整张新向量（距离，线路；数字是延迟，单位毫秒）：A 8 A、B 20 A、C 28 I、D 20 H、E 17 I、F 30 I、G 18 H、H 12 H、I 10 I、K 6 K、L 15 K。比如到 D：经 A 是 8+40=48，经 I 是 10+27=37，经 H 是 12+8=20，经 K 是 6+24=30，取 20。

title.en: Compute one round of updates
title.zh: 算一轮更新

prompt.en: Router X has three neighbours: P (link delay 3), Q (5) and R (4). The three neighbours advertise their “distance to Z” as: P reports 9, Q reports 2, R reports 6. After X updates, what are its distance and line to Z?
prompt.zh: 路由器 X 有三个邻居：P（链路延迟 3）、Q（5）、R（4）。三个邻居通告的「到 Z 的距离」分别是：P 报 9，Q 报 2，R 报 6。X 更新后，到 Z 的距离和线路是什么？

label.en: 7, via Q
label.zh: 7，经 Q

label.en: 2, via Q
label.zh: 2，经 Q

feedback.en: That took only the smallest number a neighbour reported and forgot to add the segment from X to Q (5).
feedback.zh: 只取了邻居报告的最小值，忘了加上 X 到 Q 的这一段 (5)。

label.en: 12, via P
label.zh: 12，经 P

feedback.en: P is indeed closest to X (3), but the total to Z via P is 3+9 = 12, the worst of the three routes. What you pick is the smallest total distance, not the nearest neighbour.
feedback.zh: P 虽然离 X 最近 (3)，但经 P 到 Z 总共是 3+9 = 12，是三条路里最差的。要选的是总距离最小，不是最近的邻居。

label.en: 10, via R
label.zh: 10，经 R

feedback.en: Via R it is 4+6 = 10, which is larger than via Q at 5+2 = 7.

explain.en: Each neighbour gives one candidate: via P it is 3+9 = 12, via Q it is 5+2 = 7, via R it is 4+6 = 10. Take the smallest, 7, and write Q as the line.
explain.zh: 每个邻居给一个候选值：经 P 是 3+9 = 12，经 Q 是 5+2 = 7，经 R 是 4+6 = 10。取最小的 7，线路写 Q。

hints.en: For each neighbour, first add the segment to it, then compare.
hints.zh: 对每个邻居，先加上到它的那一段，再比较。

title.en: The weak spot of distance vector: bad news travels slowly
title.zh: 距离向量的软肋：坏消息传得慢

text.en: Good news (a shorter route appears) travels one hop per round and soon spreads everywhere. Bad news (a link goes down) instead gets worse and worse as it spreads. The smallest example: three routers A—B—C in a line, each segment with weight 1. At the start, C's distance to itself is 0, B's to C is 1, and A's to C is 2 (via B).
text.zh: 好消息（出现了一条更短的路）每一轮传一跳，很快就传遍。坏消息（一条链路断了）却会越传越糟。最小的例子：三个路由器 A—B—C 连成一条线，每段权重 1。开始时 C 到自己是 0，B 到 C 是 1，A 到 C 是 2（经 B）。

text.en: Now the B—C link goes down. B loses its direct route, but it hears its neighbour A say “my distance to C is 2”, so it assumes it can get there via A: B to C = 2+1 = 3. Then A hears B say “my distance to C is 3” and updates to 4; B hears A's 4 and becomes 5... The two routers feed each other, the numbers climb round after round and never reach infinity, which is called **count to infinity**.
text.zh: 现在 B—C 链路断了。B 失去了直连的路，但它听到邻居 A 说「我到 C 是 2」，于是以为经 A 能到：B 到 C = 2+1 = 3。A 又听到 B 说「我到 C 是 3」，更新成 4；B 再听到 A 的 4，变成 5……两个路由器互相喂，数字一轮轮往上涨，永远追不上无穷大，这叫**无穷计数**（count to infinity）。

text.en: This is exactly why the slides say distance vector “converges too slowly”, and it is why link state came about.
text.zh: 这正是课件说距离向量「收敛太慢」的原因，也是链路状态出现的原因。

title.en: Beyond the slides
title.zh: 超出课件

body.en: Real protocols set a very small “infinity” (for example 16 hops) to cut the counting off, and use other tricks to ease the problem, but the root of count to infinity is that “a router believes the number its neighbour tells it, without knowing whether that number was itself obtained through the router”.
body.zh: 实际协议会设一个很小的「无穷大」（例如 16 跳）来截断计数，并用其他技巧缓解，但无穷计数的根子是「路由器只相信邻居说的数字，却不知道那个数字是不是靠自己得来的」。

title.en: Link state: everyone gets the whole map
title.zh: 链路状态：每人都拿到整张地图

text.en: Link state routing takes a different approach: instead of exchanging “computed distances”, it sends the **raw facts** (who I am connected to, and at what distance) to everyone, and each router assembles the whole graph itself and then computes. Each router does five things:
text.zh: 链路状态路由换了个思路：不交换「算出来的距离」，而是把**原始事实**（我和谁相连、距离多少）发给所有人，每个路由器自己拼出整张图再算。每个路由器做五件事：

items.en: Discover its neighbours and learn their network addresses.
items.zh: 发现邻居，学到它们的网络地址。

items.en: Measure the distance to each neighbour.
items.zh: 测量到每个邻居的距离。

items.en: Build a **link state packet** (LSP).
items.zh: 构建**链路状态包**（LSP, link state packet）。

items.en: Send the LSP to all the other routers by flooding.
items.zh: 用泛洪把 LSP 发给所有其他路由器。

items.en: Collect all the LSPs, assemble the whole graph, and use Dijkstra to compute the shortest path to every router.
items.zh: 收齐所有 LSP，拼出整张图，用 Dijkstra 算到每个路由器的最短路径。

text.en: The slides' example: six routers A–F, with the numbers being link weights.
text.zh: 课件的例子：六个路由器 A–F，数字是链路权重。

alt.en: Six routers A to F: A-B 4, A-E 5, B-C 2, B-F 6, C-E 1, C-D 3, D-F 7, E-F 8
alt.zh: 六个路由器 A 到 F：A-B 4、A-E 5、B-C 2、B-F 6、C-E 1、C-D 3、D-F 7、E-F 8

caption.en: Link weights: AB 4, AE 5, BC 2, BF 6, CD 3, CE 1, DF 7, EF 8.

text.en: Each router's LSP is just its own list of neighbours (the neighbours and the distances):
text.zh: 每个路由器的 LSP，就是它自己的邻居清单（邻居和距离）：

head.en: Neighbours and distances in the LSP
head.zh: LSP 里写的邻居和距离

text.en: Each LSP also carries two fields: the **sequence number Seq** lets routers discard duplicate and out-of-date packets (accepting only a larger sequence number), and the **age Age** lets stale packets expire on their own. An LSP is regenerated periodically, or when something major happens (a link goes down).
text.zh: 每个 LSP 还带两个字段：**序号 Seq** 让路由器丢掉重复和过期的包（只收序号更大的），**寿命 Age** 让陈旧的包自己过期消失。LSP 在定期、或发生重大事件（链路断了）时重新生成。

text.en: Having collected all six LSPs, A has assembled the graph above and runs Dijkstra: B 4, E 5, C 6 (6 either via B or via E), F 10, D 9. OSPF (Open Shortest Path First) is the link state protocol widely used on the Internet.
text.zh: 收齐六个 LSP，A 就拼出了上面这张图，再用 Dijkstra 算：B 4、E 5、C 6（经 B 或经 E 都是 6）、F 10、D 9。OSPF（Open Shortest Path First）就是互联网上广泛使用的链路状态协议。

text.en: Why does it converge faster than distance vector? Suppose C–E goes down: C and E each immediately generate a new LSP and flood it across the network. At almost the same moment, every router receives the same raw fact, “C–E is down”, and recomputes on its own. Nobody has to trust stale numbers held by a neighbour, so routers do not feed each other outdated numbers as on the previous page, and there is no count to infinity. The price is that every router stores the whole graph and runs Dijkstra once more.
text.zh: 为什么它收敛比距离向量快？假设 C–E 断了：C 和 E 立刻各生成一个新的 LSP，泛洪给全网。几乎同时，每个路由器都拿到同一个原始事实「C–E 断了」，各自重新算一遍。没有人要相信邻居手里的旧数字，所以不会像上一页那样互相喂过期的数字，也就没有无穷计数。代价是每个路由器要存整张图、多算一遍 Dijkstra。

title.en: Which one is link state?
title.zh: 哪一个是链路状态

prompt.en: A link has just gone down. Which of these descriptions belongs to link state routing rather than distance vector?
prompt.zh: 一条链路刚刚断了。下面哪一种描述属于链路状态路由，而不是距离向量？

label.en: The router that detects the broken link floods “my links to my neighbours and their distances” to the whole network, and every router that receives it reruns Dijkstra
label.zh: 检测到链路断开的路由器，把「我和各邻居的链路及距离」泛洪给全网，每个路由器收到后重新跑 Dijkstra

label.en: A router tells its whole distance table only to its neighbours, who update and then tell their own neighbours, spreading round by round
label.zh: 路由器把自己的整张距离表只告诉邻居，邻居更新后再告诉各自的邻居，一轮轮传开

feedback.en: That is distance vector: what is exchanged is computed distances, sent only to neighbours.
feedback.zh: 这是距离向量：交换的是算出来的距离，只发给邻居。

label.en: The network elects one central router, which computes the routing tables and distributes them
label.zh: 全网选出一台中心路由器，由它算好路由表再分发

feedback.en: In both algorithms every router computes for itself, with no centre.
feedback.zh: 两种算法都是每个路由器自己算，没有中心。

label.en: Every router floods out all packets and needs no routing table
label.zh: 每个路由器把所有包都泛洪出去，不需要路由表

feedback.en: That is flooding as a forwarding method, not link state. Link state floods only LSPs; data packets are still forwarded by the routing table.
feedback.zh: 这是泛洪转发，不是链路状态。链路状态只泛洪 LSP，数据包仍按路由表转发。

explain.en: Distance vector: exchanges computed distances, only with neighbours, which means less computing but slow convergence (plus count to infinity). Link state: exchanges raw link facts, flooded to everyone, so each router computes Dijkstra once more and stores the whole graph, but converges quickly.
explain.zh: 距离向量：交换算出来的距离，只发给邻居，算得少但收敛慢（还有无穷计数）。链路状态：交换原始的链路事实，泛洪给所有人，每个路由器要多算一遍 Dijkstra、多存整张图，但收敛快。

chapter.en: Scale, broadcast and the big picture

title.en: Hierarchical routing: when the network gets big, split it into regions
title.zh: 层次路由：网络大了，就分区

text.en: As a network grows, routing tables get longer and longer, and CPU and memory cannot keep up. The remedy is to divide routers into **regions**: each router knows everything about the other routers in its own region and nothing about other regions, only “to reach that region, go out on this line”; the routers that join two regions act as exits.
text.zh: 网络变大后，路由表越来越长，CPU 和内存吃不消。办法是把路由器分成**区域**（regions）：每个路由器完全了解本区域的其他路由器，对别的区域一无所知，只知道「去那个区域，从哪条线出去」；连着两个区域的路由器充当出口。

alt.zh: 五个区域：区域 1 里有 1A、1B、1C；1B 通向区域 2，1C 通向区域 3；区域 3 连区域 4，区域 4 连区域 5，区域 2 也连到区域 5

caption.en: The slides' five regions, seen from 1A.
caption.zh: 课件的五个区域，站在 1A 看。

text.en: Look from router 1A. The full table, with one row per router, has 17 entries (destination, line, hops):
text.zh: 站在路由器 1A 上看。完整的表，每台路由器一行，有 17 项（目的地、线路、跳数）：

text.en: After splitting into regions, the three rows for 1A, 1B, 1C in its own region stay as they are, and each other region is merged into one row, leaving only 7 entries:
text.zh: 分区之后，本区域的 1A、1B、1C 三行照旧，别的区域各合成一行，只有 7 项：

text.en: Read it against the full table: the Region 2 row leaves via 1B at 2 hops, which is 2A, the closest router in Region 2 to 1A; Region 3 is 3B at 2 hops, Region 4 is 4A at 3 hops, and Region 5 is 5A at 4 hops. The hop count in the hierarchical table is the hops to the nearest router in that region. 17 entries become 7, and the more regions there are, the more it saves.
text.zh: 和完整表对照着读：区域 2 一行，从 1B 出，2 跳，就是区域 2 里离 1A 最近的 2A；区域 3 是 3B 的 2 跳，区域 4 是 4A 的 3 跳，区域 5 是 5A 的 4 跳。层次表里的跳数，是到那个区域里最近一台路由器的跳数。17 项变成 7 项，每多一个区域，省得更多。

title.en: The cost: some destinations get a longer route
title.zh: 代价：有些目的地的路变长

body.en: In the full table, reaching 5C goes via 1B, 5 hops. In the hierarchical table Region 5 has only one row, which sends everything to 1C, so reaching 5C also goes via 1C. That route cannot be shorter than 5 hops, and the slides say it may be somewhat longer. Here is a small example that puts the numbers in plain view: S has two entrances into Region Y, entrance Y1 is 1 hop from S, and entrance Y2 is 2 hops from S. A destination D inside Y is 5 hops from Y1 but only 1 hop from Y2. Full table: via Y2, 2+1 = 3 hops. In the hierarchical table the single row for “Region Y” records the nearest entrance Y1, so it goes via Y1, 1+5 = 6 hops. The table is smaller, but the route is 3 hops longer.
body.zh: 完整表里，去 5C 走 1B，5 跳。层次表里区域 5 只有一行，一律交给 1C，所以去 5C 也走 1C。这条路不可能比 5 跳更短，课件说它可能略长。用一个小例子把数字摆在明面上：S 通往区域 Y 有两个入口，入口 Y1 离 S 1 跳，入口 Y2 离 S 2 跳。Y 里的目的地 D，离 Y1 有 5 跳，离 Y2 只有 1 跳。完整表：经 Y2，2+1 = 3 跳。层次表里「区域 Y」一行，记的是最近的入口 Y1，走 Y1，1+5 = 6 跳。表小了，路却多出 3 跳。

title.en: The same idea as CIDR
title.zh: 和 CIDR 是同一个想法

body.en: CIDR in Lesson 9 aggregates many addresses into one prefix, so one routing table row stands for a large block of addresses; hierarchical routing aggregates many routers into one region, so one row stands for a whole region. One works on addresses, the other on routers. The Internet's counterpart to a “region” is the Autonomous System.
body.zh: 第 9 课的 CIDR 把许多地址聚合成一个前缀，路由表里一行代表一大片地址；层次路由把许多路由器聚合成一个区域，一行代表一整个区域。一个作用于地址，一个作用于路由。互联网上类似「区域」的单位是自治系统（Autonomous System）。

title.en: How many entries in the hierarchical table?
title.zh: 层次表有几项

prompt.en: A network has 6 regions, each with 8 routers. A router in Region 1 has a full table of 48 entries. After switching to hierarchical routing, how many entries does its table have?
prompt.zh: 一个网络有 6 个区域，每个区域有 8 台路由器。区域 1 里的一台路由器，完整表有 48 项。改用层次路由后，它的表有几项？

hints.en: Each router in its own region takes one entry (including itself); for each other region, the whole region takes just one entry.
hints.zh: 本区域的每台路由器各占一项（包括它自己）；别的区域，每个区域只占一项。

explain.en: The 8 routers in its own region take one entry each, 8 in all; the other 5 regions take one entry each, 5 in all. 8+5 = 13 entries, far fewer than 48. In the slides, 1A's table shrinking from 17 entries to 7 follows the same calculation: 3+4 = 7. The cost is that for other regions it only records “which line to leave by”, so the route to some destinations gets longer.
explain.zh: 本区域 8 台路由器各一项，共 8 项；另外 5 个区域各一项，共 5 项。8+5 = 13 项，远小于 48。课件里 1A 的表从 17 项缩到 7 项，也是同一个算法：3+4 = 7。代价是去别的区域时只记「从哪条线出去」，有些目的地的路会变长。

title.en: Broadcast routing and reverse path forwarding
title.zh: 广播路由与反向路径转发

text.en: Sometimes one host needs to send a message to all the other hosts. There are four ways:
text.zh: 有时要让一台主机把消息发给所有其他主机。有四种办法：

items.en: Send a separate packet to each destination: inefficient, and the source has to know all the destination addresses.
items.zh: 给每个目的地发一个单独的包：低效，而且源要知道所有目的地址。

items.en: **Multi-destination routing**: the packet carries a list of destination addresses, and each router splits the packet according to the best outgoing line for each destination and makes one copy for each. It saves more bandwidth than the previous method, but the source still has to know all the destination addresses.
items.zh: **多目的地路由**（multi-destination routing）：包里装着目的地址表，路由器按各目的地的最佳出线把包拆开、各复制一份。比前一种省带宽，源仍要知道所有目的地址。

items.en: **Flooding**: no need to know the destinations, but there are many duplicate packets.
items.zh: **泛洪**：不用知道目的地，但重复包很多。

items.en: **Reverse path forwarding**: explained below.
items.zh: **反向路径转发**（reverse path forwarding）：下面讲。

text.en: The rule of reverse path forwarding is simple: a router checks whether the packet arrived on **the line it normally uses to send packets to the broadcast source**.
text.zh: 反向路径转发的规则很简单：路由器检查包是不是从**平常用来给广播源发包的那条线**到达的。

items.en: Yes: that line is very likely the best path to the source, so this packet is very likely the first copy. The router copies it and forwards it on all the other lines.
items.zh: 是：这条线很可能是到源的最佳路径，所以这个包很可能是第一份拷贝。路由器复制它，从所有其他线转发出去。

items.en: No: this packet is most likely a duplicate that came by a detour, so discard it.
items.zh: 不是：这个包多半是绕路来的重复，丢弃。

alt.zh: 源 S 直连路由器 R（线路 L1，R 平常去 S 走这条），同时经路由器 X 绕到 R（线路 L2）；R 还连着 T 和 U。第一份拷贝从 L1 到达，被转发；第二份从 L2 到达，被丢弃

caption.en: Two copies of the same broadcast arrive at R.
caption.zh: 同一个广播的两份拷贝到达 R。

text.en: It is only a **heuristic** (the rule says “very likely”), and the benefit is that routers do not need to know the whole broadcast tree, only their own routing table toward the source.
text.zh: 它只是**启发式**（说的是「很可能」），好处是路由器不需要知道整棵广播树，只要有自己到源的路由表就行。

title.en: Beyond the slides
title.zh: 超出课件

body.en: More economical methods include spanning tree broadcast (forwarding only along one spanning tree, with no duplicates) and multicast (sending only to the group of hosts that want to receive). For the exam, stick to the four methods above.
body.zh: 更省的办法有生成树广播（只沿一棵生成树转发，没有重复）和组播（只发给想收的一组主机）。考试以上面四种为准。

title.en: Two copies arrive
title.zh: 收到两份拷贝

prompt.en: Router R normally sends packets to broadcast source S on line L1. Two copies of the same broadcast arrive at R: the first from L1, the second from L2. How does reverse path forwarding handle them?
prompt.zh: 路由器 R 平常发给广播源 S 的包走线路 L1。同一个广播的两份拷贝到了 R：第一份从 L1 来，第二份从 L2 来。反向路径转发怎么处理？

label.en: Copy the first and forward it on all lines other than L1; discard the second
label.zh: 第一份复制并从 L1 以外的所有线转发，第二份丢弃

label.en: Forward both on all the other lines
label.zh: 两份都从所有其他线转发出去

feedback.en: That would be plain flooding, and duplicates would pile up.
feedback.zh: 那就成了普通泛洪，重复包会越来越多。

label.en: Discard both, because they are duplicates
label.zh: 两份都丢弃，因为收到了重复

feedback.en: The first must be forwarded, otherwise the broadcast cannot spread. The difference is which line it came from, not how many copies arrived.
feedback.zh: 第一份要转发，否则广播传不下去。区别在于它是从哪条线来的，不是收到几份。

label.en: First check the whole broadcast tree, and forward only after confirming the path is right
label.zh: 先查整棵广播树，确认路径正确再转发

feedback.en: The point of reverse path forwarding is that it does not need to know the whole tree; it only checks whether the arrival line is the one that leads to the source.
feedback.zh: 反向路径转发的好处就是不需要知道整棵树，只看到达的线是不是去源的那条线。

explain.en: The one from L1 came along the usual best path to S and is very likely the first copy to arrive, so forward it; the one from L2 is a duplicate that came by a detour, so drop it. This is only “very likely”, which is why it is a heuristic.
explain.zh: 从 L1 来的，走的是平常到 S 的最佳路径，很可能是最先到的拷贝，转发；从 L2 来的是绕路的重复，丢。这只是「很可能」，所以是启发式。

title.en: Overview: addresses and routing, all the way through
title.zh: 总览：地址和路由，一路走完

text.en: First half: running out of addresses
text.zh: 上半场：地址不够用

rows.en: Private addresses plus NAT: inside, everyone uses private addresses; going out, they are swapped for one public address, and port numbers tell connections apart
rows.zh: 私有地址加 NAT：内部各用私有地址，出站时换成一个公网地址，用端口号区分连接

rows.en: People outside cannot connect in; it breaks layering
rows.zh: 外面不能主动连进来；违反分层

rows.en: The address space is simply not big enough
IPv6: 128-bit addresses, a fixed 40-byte header; transition by dual stack, tunneling, header translation
rows.zh: IPv6：128 位地址，头部固定 40 字节；过渡靠双栈、隧道、头部翻译

rows.en: It has to coexist with IPv4 for a very long time
rows.zh: 要和 IPv4 共存很长一段时间

rows.en: Just joined the network and have nothing
DHCP gets an IP and gateway, ARP turns an IP into a MAC, ICMP reports back (ping, traceroute)
rows.zh: DHCP 领 IP 和网关，ARP 把 IP 换成 MAC，ICMP 报信 (ping、traceroute)

text.en: Back to that one click: the laptop joins Wi-Fi, first uses DHCP to get a private address and ARP to find the gateway's MAC; as the packet leaves, NAT swaps your address and port for the dorm's public address; after that, the router at every hop forwards by its routing table. The second half is about how that table gets built.
text.zh: 回到那一次点击：笔记本连上 Wi-Fi，先用 DHCP 领到一个私有地址，用 ARP 找到网关的 MAC；包出门时，NAT 把你的地址和端口换成宿舍的公网地址；之后每一跳的路由器，都按路由表转发。下半场讲的，就是这张表怎么建出来。

text.en: Second half: routing
text.zh: 下半场：路由

rows.en: The whole graph is known; compute the optimal path
rows.zh: 已知整张图，算最优路径

rows.en: Needs global knowledge; does not update itself when the network changes
rows.zh: 要知道全局；网络变了不会自己更新

rows.en: Must be delivered, broadcast, sending LSPs
Many duplicate packets; needs hop and sequence number limits
rows.zh: 重复包多，需要跳数和序号限制

rows.en: Exchanges only with neighbours; slow convergence, bad news travels slowly (count to infinity)
rows.zh: 只和邻居交换；收敛慢，坏消息传得慢（无穷计数）

rows.en: Large networks, widely used on the Internet
rows.zh: 大网络，互联网上广泛使用

rows.en: Stores the whole graph, runs Dijkstra extra, flooding LSPs has overhead
rows.zh: 要存整张图、多算 Dijkstra，泛洪 LSP 有开销

rows.en: Must avoid duplicates; reverse path forwarding is only a heuristic
rows.zh: 要避免重复；反向路径转发只是启发式
较大（每个路由器跑 Dijkstra）
